subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Boston Tea Party and Coffee's Rise
description: Learn The Boston Tea Party and Coffee's Rise in one minute.

hook.text: After the Boston Tea Party in 1773, drinking tea became unpatriotic. America switched to coffee overnight.

buildup.text: Colonial anger over British tea taxes turned coffee into a symbol of independence and rebellion.

discovery.text: The Green Dragon Tavern in Boston—which also served coffee—is where revolutionaries planned the Tea Party itself.

twist.text: America's coffee preference outlasted the revolution by 250 years. One protest permanently shaped a nation's drinking habits.

climax.text: By 1830, Americans consumed the most coffee per capita of any country. The shift from tea was total.

punchline.text: A tax protest made coffee America's drink—and it never looked back.

quiz.question: Why did Americans switch from tea to coffee?
options: Drinking tea became unpatriotic after the Boston Tea Party protest against British taxes

details.summary: When American colonists dumped British tea into Boston Harbor in 1773, coffee became the patriotic alternative. Drinking coffee was a political statement against British taxation. This moment helped establish coffee as America's national drink, a preference that persists over 250 years later.
details.whyItMatters: The Boston Tea Party shows how political events can permanently redirect a nation's beverage culture. American coffee dominance traces directly to this protest.
takeaways: The 1773 Boston Tea Party made coffee a patriotic drink
Colonists rejected tea to protest British taxation
Coffee became America's national drink as a direct result

faq.question: Did Americans drink coffee before the Boston Tea Party?
faq.answer: Yes, but tea was more popular. Coffeehouses existed in major colonial cities since the late 1600s. After the Tea Party, the Continental Congress declared tea unpatriotic and coffee drinking surged as an act of political identity. The preference stuck permanently.

faq.question: How did the Boston Tea Party affect global coffee trade?
faq.answer: American demand for coffee grew steadily after independence, eventually making the United States the world's largest coffee importer. This demand fueled the expansion of coffee plantations in Latin America, particularly Brazil, reshaping the economies of the entire Western Hemisphere.
